subject.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics

question: Should the trusted inbound-decoration contract live as top-level bareBody/inboundDecorated fields or under an OpenClaw-owned metadata slot such as __openclaw.inboundDecoration?
rationale: Both shapes can solve the linked issue, but they expose different durable message contracts to readers and plugins, and automation should not choose that permanent field ownership.

options.title: Use OpenClaw-owned metadata
options.body: Move the trusted body under an explicit OpenClaw metadata owner to keep the generic message shape narrower while preserving the trusted contract.

options.title: Accept top-level fields
options.body: Keep the current PR shape if maintainers intentionally want bareBody and inboundDecorated as broader runtime and serialized message fields.

options.title: Defer contract shape
options.body: Pause the PR until the canonical issue settles the public/plugin API implications of the field location.

recommendation.title: Use OpenClaw-owned metadata
recommendation.body: Move the trusted body under an explicit OpenClaw metadata owner to keep the generic message shape narrower while preserving the trusted contract.
